text.tspan: Show all your work for each part of the question. The parts within the question may not have equal weight.
Students are given a clear, rigid cylindrical container that is sealed with a movable piston. The piston slides with
negligible friction and can be locked in place. The container is filled with one mole of a gas and can be placed in a
cold-water bath to keep the temperature of the gas constant. The students have access to a meterstick and a
pressure sensor that can be placed inside the container. They are asked to determine if the relationship between the
pressure and the volume of the gas is consistent with the ideal gas law.
Describe
an experimental procedure the students could use to collect the data needed to determine if the
relationship between the pressure and the volume of the gas is consistent with the ideal gas law. Provide enough
detail so that another student could replicate the experiment, including any steps necessary to reduce experimental
uncertainty.
Describe
how the students should analyze the data to determine if the relationship between the pressure and
the volume of the gas is consistent with the ideal gas law.
In another experiment, the students fill the container with an ideal gas and lock the piston in place so that the
volume remains fixed at
. They want to experimentally determine the number
of moles of gas
in the container. They slowly raise the temperature of the water bath and periodically measure the temperature
of the gas and the pressure
of the gas. The results are shown in the table.
i.
Indicate
two quantities that could be graphed to yield a straight line whose slope could be used to determine
the number
of moles of gas in the container. Use the blank columns in the table to list any calculated
quantities you will graph other than the data provided.
Vertical axis__________Horizontal axis__________
ii. On the grid below,
plot
the appropriate quantities to determine the number
of moles of gas inside the
container. Clearly scale and label all axes, including appropriate units.
